sentences: I check the subject and the verb in each clause to make sure they agree in number.
I keep every verb form in a paragraph referring to the same time frame unless the meaning requires a shift.
I place a comma before a coordinating conjunction when it joins two independent clauses.
I join a dependent clause to an independent clause to build a complex sentence.
I make sure that each pronoun clearly points back to one specific noun earlier in the text.
I choose between a, an, and the based on whether a noun is specific or general.
I put the preposition before its object when I build a prepositional phrase.
I use a subordinating conjunction to introduce a dependent clause that modifies the main clause.
I decide whether a word describes a noun or an action to pick an adjective or an adverb.
I mark words ending in -ing that serve as nouns inside a sentence and label them gerunds.
I move a misplaced modifier so it sits directly beside the word it describes.
I rewrite a passive clause in the active voice by putting the doer first.
I write the base form of the verb after words like demand, suggest, or require in a that-clause.
I give every item in a list the same grammatical shape so the series reads as parallel.
I look for a subject and a verb in every group of words to avoid a fragment.
I fix a run-on by separating two independent clauses with a period, a semicolon, or a conjunction.
I capitalize the first word of a sentence and every proper noun such as a name or place.
I put quotation marks around a direct quotation and place the period inside the closing mark.
I add an apostrophe to a noun to show ownership and to a verb to form a contraction.
I join two independent clauses with a semicolon when no conjunction appears between them.
